quests.sentence: Revenue dipped last quarter, but leadership isn't panicking yet.
quests.hint: This describes a completed result from a finished period.
quests.explanation: Dipped is the simple past form, describing a completed change during a finished quarter.

quests.sentence: They've quietly brought in three new advisors to shore up the strategy.
quests.hint: There's no time word, but this is recent and clearly still shaping the current situation.
quests.explanation: Have brought in is the present perfect form, describing a recent action that remains relevant to the present.

quests.sentence: Analysts think the numbers will look very different at the next earnings call.
quests.hint: This is a prediction about a future event.
quests.explanation: Will look is the simple future form, describing a predicted future outcome.

quests.sentence: He hadn't touched a paintbrush in years, yet something about that empty wall pulled him back in.
quests.hint: This lack of activity stretches back before the moment something changed.
quests.explanation: Hadn't touched is the negative past perfect form, describing a long absence of activity before a later past event.

quests.sentence: He spent the entire weekend covering it in color.
quests.hint: This is the main action described as a single completed stretch of time.
quests.explanation: Spent is the simple past form, describing a completed action over the weekend.

quests.sentence: Neighbors keep stopping by just to look at it.
quests.hint: 'Keep stopping by' points to a repeated pattern, not one visit.
quests.explanation: Keep is the simple present form, describing a repeated habitual action.

quests.sentence: Two of the senior partners haven't spoken directly in weeks.
quests.hint: There's no 'since' here, but this situation is ongoing and unresolved right now.
quests.explanation: Haven't spoken is the negative present perfect form, describing a situation continuing up to the present.

quests.sentence: Everyone else in the office has picked a side without saying so out loud.
quests.hint: This describes a current state resulting from something that has already happened.
quests.explanation: Has picked is the present perfect form, connecting a completed action to a present situation.

quests.sentence: Something's going to give before the quarter is even over.
quests.hint: The tension building right now is the evidence behind this prediction.
quests.explanation: Is going to give uses going to for a prediction based on visible current tension; notice 'is over', inside the before-clause, stays present even though it refers to the future.

quests.sentence: Someone had wiped the security footage clean before anyone thought to check it.
quests.hint: The wiping happened before anyone even had the idea to look.
quests.explanation: Had wiped is the past perfect form, showing an action completed before a later past event.

quests.sentence: Detectives spent the better part of a week chasing dead ends.
quests.hint: This describes a completed stretch of investigative work.
quests.explanation: Spent is the simple past form, describing a completed period of activity.

quests.sentence: A single overlooked receipt is about to change everything.
quests.hint: This describes something on the very edge of happening, right at this moment.
quests.explanation: Is about to change is the near-future form, describing something expected to happen at any moment.

quests.sentence: She'd never needed glasses before that particular birthday.
quests.hint: This lack of need stretches back before a specific past milestone.
quests.explanation: Had never needed (shortened to 'd never needed) is the past perfect form, describing a past experience, or the lack of one, before a later point.

quests.sentence: Reading the fine print on anything has become a small daily struggle.
quests.hint: This describes a gradual change that has led to the current situation.
quests.explanation: Has become is the present perfect form, describing a change over time that remains true now.

quests.sentence: Give it another few years, and she'll be reaching for readers just to check her phone.
quests.hint: Picture that future stretch of time — the habit will already be in place by then.
quests.explanation: Will be reaching is the future progressive form, describing an action expected to be ongoing at a future time.

quests.sentence: The riverbank has crept closer to the old mill with every passing spring.
quests.hint: This describes a gradual change over repeated periods, still continuing.
quests.explanation: Has crept is the present perfect form, describing a change that has developed over a period leading up to now.

quests.sentence: City engineers hadn't accounted for this rate of erosion when they built the original wall.
quests.hint: This oversight goes back to before the wall was even built.
quests.explanation: Hadn't accounted for is the negative past perfect form, describing an earlier gap before a later past action.

quests.sentence: Within a decade, that wall will be doing far more work than it was ever designed for.
quests.hint: Picture that future decade — the situation will already be ongoing by then.
quests.explanation: Will be doing is the future progressive form, describing an ongoing situation expected at a future time.

quests.sentence: Something had shifted between them long before anyone else noticed.
quests.hint: The shift happened well before it became visible to others, an earlier point.
quests.explanation: Had shifted is the past perfect form, describing a change that occurred before a later past realization.

quests.sentence: Holidays got quieter after that, though nobody ever said exactly why.
quests.hint: This describes a change that followed a completed earlier event.
quests.explanation: Got is the simple past form, describing a change that took place in the past.

quests.sentence: These days, they've settled into something calmer, if a little distant.
quests.hint: This is a recent development still shaping the present situation.
quests.explanation: Have settled is the present perfect form, connecting a recent change to the current situation.

quests.sentence: The team had been training the model on outdated data for months before anyone flagged the drop in accuracy.
quests.hint: This measures how long the problem had continued before it was noticed.
quests.explanation: Had been training is the past perfect progressive form, emphasizing a continuing process before a later past discovery.

quests.sentence: A junior analyst noticed the pattern almost by accident.
quests.hint: This is the specific discovery, told as a completed event.
quests.explanation: Noticed is the simple past form, describing a single completed past action.

quests.sentence: Engineers are quietly rebuilding the pipeline from scratch.
quests.hint: There's no time marker, but this describes an ongoing project happening right now.
quests.explanation: Are rebuilding is the present progressive form, describing a project currently in progress.

quests.sentence: By the time critics finally came around, he'd already walked away from the sport entirely.
quests.hint: His retirement happened before the critics' change of heart, an earlier point.
quests.explanation: Had walked away (shortened to 'd walked away) is the past perfect form, showing this happened before a later past event.

quests.sentence: Injuries had worn him down long before the losses started piling up.
quests.hint: The wearing-down process happened well before the losing streak began.
quests.explanation: Had worn down is the past perfect form, describing an earlier cause behind a later past development.

quests.sentence: Some say the records he set will stand for another generation.
quests.hint: This is a prediction about how long something will remain true.
quests.explanation: Will stand is the will-future form, describing a prediction about the future.

quests.sentence: Nobody had said the word out loud yet, but everyone in that room already knew.
quests.hint: The unspoken silence stretches back before the moment being described.
quests.explanation: Had said is the past perfect form; combined with 'nobody', it describes something that had not yet happened before a later past state.

quests.sentence: The silence afterward said more than any of them expected.
quests.hint: This is a single completed reflection on what happened.
quests.explanation: Said is the simple past form, describing a completed past event.

quests.sentence: Whatever happens next, this version of the team is finished.
quests.hint: This describes a current, settled state, regardless of what the future holds.
quests.explanation: Is finished is the simple present form, describing a current state rather than an action.
